title: How much water is in an answer?
summary: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning separates an agent's high-volume execution work from frontier planning, while a Water Research article forces a more exact accounting of direct, electricity-linked, and semiconductor water use. The rundown covers ChatGPT's ad expansion, exposed encrypted reasoning traces, Mistral's regional inference, Go's case for reviewable agent-written code, Unsloth Desktop, and the Daybreak models on AWS.

threads.name: Data-center buildout backlash
threads.status: A Water Research synthesis now frames AI water demand as three separate accounts—on-site cooling, electricity generation, and semiconductor manufacturing—and argues for water-conscious siting plus facility-level disclosure; its global projection remains an estimate rather than a local meter reading.
threads.arc: The thread advances from public promises about data-center water to the accounting needed to test them, with attention shifting from one global total toward facility, watershed, source, and time.

dives.story: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as the execution tier in a routed agent system
dives.why_it_matters: Teams operating long-running agents need to know whether a smaller, sparse, customizable model can cut the cost and latency of repetitive tool work without allowing misrouting or correlated self-validation to turn a small quality gap into long-horizon drift.

dives.story: The three-part water footprint of AI and the limits of one per-prompt number
dives.why_it_matters: Communities hosting data centers, infrastructure buyers, and cloud customers need water claims tied to a facility, watershed, source, month, and accounting boundary before projections can guide permits, procurement, or workload placement.

concepts_taught: AI water-footprint accounting as three joined ledgers—direct facility cooling and humidification, indirect water associated with electricity generation, and embodied semiconductor-manufacturing water—plus why withdrawal, consumption, source, watershed, time, and water-use effectiveness must remain visible rather than collapsing into one per-prompt constant

execution-tier model routing for long-running agents: route bounded repetitive work to a smaller sparse model, preserve deterministic postconditions and escalation paths, evaluate end-to-end task time rather than token speed alone, and shadow-test task families before promotion
